draft_email:
I'm trying to reach whoever looks after telecommunications or infrastructure at Sekala Private Game Lodge — apologies if this lands with the wrong person.

My name is Gerhard Smith from CTTX Services. We design and install private wireless infrastructure for farms, lodges, and reserves across South Africa.

I did a preliminary desktop review of Sekala Private Game Lodge in Welgevonden and wanted to share what I found before reaching out.

The Waterberg terrain around the reserve ranges from roughly 1,080 m (north/gate area) to 1,800 m (southern plateau), which is classic line-of-sight territory — the plateau edges and ridgelines in the area are the kind of geography where a properly positioned relay can reach properties that satellite or standard cellular cannot serve well.

Vaalwater is approximately 24 km to the north. WaterbergNET operates fixed-wireless infrastructure out of Vaalwater, and the key question is whether there is a viable elevated relay point between town and the property.

Welgevonden has multiple commercial lodges (Makweti Safari Lodge, Ekuthuleni Lodge, Tshwene Lodge and others) all facing the same last-mile challenge. If the terrain allows, a shared infrastructure arrangement across the reserve makes more sense technically and commercially than each property solving this independently.

Beyond guest Wi-Fi, the applications worth looking at for a property like this include guest Wi-Fi across multiple buildings, ranger/staff comms, remote camera/CCTV, property management systems — the sort of backbone that makes remote management and security practical.

I am not proposing a solution at this stage. The desktop review identifies whether a proper assessment is worth doing.

If connectivity across the property is something you're looking at, I'd be happy to walk you through what the preliminary desktop review found and explain what a formal infrastructure assessment would establish.

A short call is usually enough to determine whether it's worth taking further.
